headline: Computational models predict cancer pathway, antibody kinetics and codon design outcomes
label: Computational Molecular Systems Modeling
summary: Recent preprints apply GPU simulation, metadynamics and Bayesian networks to forecast molecular and pathway behavior in silico.
synthesis: The dominant thread is in silico prediction of molecular and pathway behavior from computational models rather than direct wet-lab measurement. FLAME GPU 2 agent-based simulation is applied to MAPK/ERK signaling with BRAFV600E and cFos nuclear dynamics, and a probabilistic dynamic Bayesian network models multi-fault behavior across GF and MAPK pathways, ranking known-drug combinations. MAHLER pairs inverse-folding models with metadynamics to predict relative antibody-antigen dissociation kinetics across point mutants. ASTEROID, a spatiotemporal Transformer with local-global attention, forecasts multi-step atomic coordinates of molecular dynamics trajectories while avoiding iterative integration. Codon optimization of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein is recast as Ising-model sampling for thermodynamic hardware and benchmarked against a genetic algorithm. What is new is the substitution of learned or sampling-based surrogates for iterative simulation or search, applied across heterogeneous model classes and hardware.
